messages:
jun: Quick help — trying to find all logs for request_id=abc123-2026 and trace=1a2b3c. Console trace view only shows a short span and headers are collapsed. Need the full request lines from edge -> service pods. Any quick CLI + console tips?

maria: paste the exact ids if you can, and which cluster/namespace? edge sometimes rewrites the header.

jun: namespace=prod, cluster=us-west-2. request_id=abc123-2026, trace=1a2b3c.

observability-bot: trace created: https://console.redwood.internal/traces/1a2b3c (may be sampled) :link:

ben: two quick paths: console and stern/kubectl. Console: open Traces -> click trace id -> on spans pane use the "Show raw" button to see headers. If header is missing, try the raw request logs view.

sasha: CLI tip — if you want to scan edge logs first:
```
stern -n prod edge --since 1h | rg "abc123-2026"
# or
kubectl logs -n prod deploy/edge -c envoy --since=1h | rg "abc123-2026"
```
This finds the header as rewritten by envoy.

maria: also try matching on trace id in logs: some services log trace.id as span_id or trace_id depending on lib. Example query in our logs UI: `json.trace_id: \"1a2b3c\" OR json.request_id: \"abc123-2026\"`

oliver: small gotcha — we sample traces at 10% for high-traffic paths, so trace link might exist but be sparse. If the trace is missing, map via span ids you find in service logs and then search for those spans in the traces UI.

jun: running stern now...

jun: stern returned lines from edge-12 and I can see an upstream host and the x-request-id still present. Extracted the upstream request_id and matched on pod logs for svc-a.

ben: if you need to jump straight from trace to pod logs: click the span, use the "Associated logs" link (if available) — it opens the logs UI pre-filtered. If it doesn't exist, copy the span.timestamp and run a time-bounded search in logs (+- 30s).

maria: runbook snippet to add for others:
```
1. Check Traces -> paste trace id -> expand spans -> click "Show raw"
2. If headers collapsed: go to Logs UI -> query json.request_id OR json.trace_id
3. If still missing: stern -n <ns> <edge-pod> | rg <request_id>
4. From edge pod log, extract upstream host/pod and then kubectl logs for that pod with a narrow time window
```

oliver: FYI I added a dashboard card that links traces -> logs for the edge service, helps with these exact cases. See: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/edge-tracing-quicklinks

jun: thanks all — found the error in svc-a logs (timeout on downstream call). tagging @sre for potential retry/backoff tune :thumbsup:

sasha: nice. If this is recurring, open an alert request in #incidents with the query and suggested threshold; I can help tune the alerting window.

ben: final tip: when console collapses fields, click the three-dot menu on the span and choose "Show JSON" — saves time vs guessing which header key was used.

jun: awesome, will follow up with a short postmortem in the ticket.

maria: added a short guide to the eng-runtime docs with the stern snippets and links. Thanks!
